recipes.name: Chocolate Trifle
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.9 ounce) package instant chocolate pudding mix
1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed
1 (12 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9-inch square glass baking pan.
Combine brownie mix, egg, 1/4 cup water, and vegetable oil in a large bowl. Stir until well-blended, about 50 strokes. Spread into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted 1 inch in from the edges comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool completely, about 30 mintues.
Cut cooled brownies into 1-inch squares and set aside.
Combine condensed milk, remaining 1/2 cup water, and pudding mix in a large bowl; mix until smooth. Fold in 8 ounces whipped topping until no streaks remain.

Place 1/2 of the brownies in a trifle bowl or glass serving dish. Top with 1/2 of the pudding mixture, then 1/2 of the 12-ounce container of whipped topping. Repeat layers. Shave chocolate on top for garnish.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Trifle
raw_recipe.description: This pretty chocolate trifle with layers of fudgy brownies, rich and creamy chocolate pudding, and fluffy whipped topping is chilled to perfection.

video.description: See how easy it is to create an impressive chocolate trifle dessert. Layers of brownies, chocolate pudding, and whipped topping combine to create a chocolate-lover’s delight.

review.reviewBody:
WOW!

I made this two times - once exactly according to recipe, and second with a few alterations.

The recipe version was fantastic, and I did not think it was too sweet. It was very rich, and I thought there was a strong cool whip flavor, and not enough chocolate. Nonetheless, it was delicious and everyone agreed.

The second time I followed some suggestions here, and the dessert won me first place in a contest this weekend! I mixed the pudding and water, and in a separate bowl whipped 1/2 pint heavy cream and 3 tbsp sugar, then folded in the cream with the pudding/water. I also did use the french vanilla cool whip in place of the plain (12 oz). So, I layered brownies, caramel, heath toffee bits, chocolate whipped cream, and french vanilla cool whip. Repeat!

It was PHENOMENAL. I had so many requests for the recipe, and I saw numerous people going back for 2nds and 3rds. It was a major hit, and will be a staple dessert dish for me!

Thank you!!

This review is a little late but this recipe is EXCELLENT! I made it first for a fake thanksgiving a week early with family that was going out of town, it was very good, but I don't like whipped topping and I found it had entirely too much of that. So i made it again for Thanksgiving the next week and it was soooo amazing! But I made a few adjustments... in the brownie layer I addred about half a bottle of caramel topping (as you would use on ice cream) in the brownie pan before it went into the oven. (really good...) then in the pudding layer, instead of folding in the whipped topping, i bought half a pint of heavy whipping cream and whipped that for about 10 minutes myself and then folded that into the pudding. It made such an incredible difference. The pudding tasted so mych richer, like custard, instead of fluffy like whipped topping. I also added bailey's in the pudding and cut strawberries, chocolate chunks - per my husband's request, and toffee bits, which made it look so pretty. But you can add pretty much anything you want and it still tastes EXCELLENT! EVERYONE who tried it loved it and my mother-in-law asked for the recipe, along with everyone else. Always nice to confirm that her son didn't make a mistake marrying me:-) YOU HAVE TO TRY THIS DESSERT, YUMMMMM!!!!!!!!!!!!!

This recipe was a success for me. Changes: We omitted the sweetened condensed milk and used REAL homemade whipped cream. Real whip cream is so delicious, so I recommend going for the real thing! I read another review that mentioned not liking the synthetic taste of the cool whip and instant pudding. I can relate as I prefer fresh ingredients too. I might try this with cooked pudding in the future. I don’t own a trifle container, so I used a pretty, glass salad bowl and had a bit left over to put in a small individual sized glass salad bowl. The chocolate trifle is rich and elegant, so we made small servings. I topped it off with a high quality salted carmel chocolate bar, broken in large pieces. PS: As one reviewer suggested, I mixed whipped cream with pudding for one of the layers.

The only reason I didn't give this 5 stars was I used a number of the suggestions of other reviews. I whipped 1 cup of heavy whipping cream and added that to the sweetened condensed milk and pudding mix. I used a brownie mix that contained dark chocolate chips and baked it in a 7" X 11" pan so the brownie pieces would be thinner. I cut them in small pieces and broke them up a little but didn't crumble them. I was concerned the outside edges were too hard but they added a nice texture and were softened by the pudding mixture. I drizzled caramel sauce on top of the brownies and sprinkled on toffee bits. I couldn't find French vanilla Cool Whip so I added vanilla extract to the regular and it turned out great. It was a big hit at our Church homegroup potluck and I loved it. I've never used the words "too" and "sweet" together so I thought it was wonderful and it got rave reviews. Thanks for posting this!

This was a show stopper - the perfect, light, fluffy end to a heavy holiday meal. I took other's advice and used heavy whipping cream (whipped with an electric mixer in no time) with some confectioner's sugar for both folding in the pudding and also the whipped cream layer. I did add a layer, made with fresh raspberries and some seedless raspberry jam - wow, that was amazing - both for color and for taste. For the presentation, I used raspberries, small pieces of brownies, all dusted (using a sifter) with confectioner's sugar. It was a HIT!

The pudding in this is so easy to make and while it isn't mousse, it isn't supposed to be! Easy modifications are endless with this. I made a Devil's Food chocolate cake in a cookie sheet instead of brownies because I didn't have any brownie mix. I drizzled chocolate syrup on half the cake to make it gooey yummy, and Bailey's Irish Crème on the other half. I used the chocolate syrup cake layer first, pudding next and on top of the pudding I added crushed oreo's and sliced strawberry's. Then the Cool Whip. Repeated with the Bailey's flavored cake next. I topped the last Cool Whip with shaved chocolate and some strawberries for decoration. It took some time, but real easy and YES! A crowd pleaser!

Thanks for this recipe. I made a few modifications because I do not like the taste of Coolwhip and evaporated milk would have been too sweet. Instead I whipped up a 473 mL carton of whipping cream and added 3 Tbsp sugar and a generous amount of vanilla. I folded in about 2 cups of this with the pudding and omitted the evaporated milk. I also included a cherry pie filling layer in between the pudding layer and whipped cream layer. This came out delicious and was devoured by my family.

Made 20 individual trifles using 7-8 oz. plastic serving dishes. Perfect amount. I used freshly whipped cream and gluten free brownies, since many in the group are GF. Topped with 1/2 a strawberry. It's more work but individual servings are often better with a buffet meal. The trifle stays a trifle instead of a blob on a piece of key lime pie.

Hi! I made this twice. And I loved it. After reading the recipe I knew I would make a couple of changes. I used a brownie recipe that used chocolate chips which made for nice little chunks of chocolate in the trifle. I also made stabilized whipped cream, instead of using store-bought, which makes such a huge difference. AND, I drizzled a little dulce de leche over the brownie layer. The first time I made this I served it after 8 or so hours in the refrigerator. This really is at its best after 24 hours or so. The second time I made it I prepared it on Thursday evening for Saturday afternoon, and it was perfect! The chocolate has a chance to mellow, the flavors have a chance to marry, and the texture is great. Thanks for the recipe, Wayne!

Made this recipe & it turned out really well, but by accident and by choice, I didn't follow directions exactly, but similarly, so my review is based on how I made it.

My husband bought the larger package of pudding mix, so I mixed that with the condensed milk (only one can even though mix was equivalent to 2 of the size asked for), and mixed until it thickened a bit. We do not use or eat Cool Whip, so I used real whipped cream, that I made with vanilla and icing sugar. I was too lazy & didn't have time to make brownies, so used store bought ones we like.

It is very rich but was delicious (I have a pretty sweet tooth too, especially with chocolate) & my kids have already requested I make it again.

Made with a few changes.

First, I felt like the Cool Whip/SCMilk layer sounded way too sweet, so I made the pudding as the package directed with milk and then folded it into a tub of cool whip.

Second, I used Snickers as my candy, and it was more like two full bars. One handful reserved for garnish, one handful layered (around the edge against the glass for visual effect) in the middle of the layers, and the rested stirred into the plain cool whip WITH three chopped, peeled Granny Smith apples to add crunch and cut the sweetness a bit. 

So yeah, it wasn't much this recipe after all. But it was a good jumping off point!

This is my favorite "go-to" dessert! I used to just do the chocolate but now I am venturing out to different flavors. I have done the brownies with banana pudding, pound cake or angel food cake with lemon pudding and fresh blueberries, and strawberry cake with chocolate pudding and fresh strawberries. There are so many potential variations! I also make my own whipped cream for this. This is an amazing recipe!
I only modified a few things. I added dark chocolate wafer to the top of the first layer and a butterfinger bar to the top. I used Cool Whip for the pudding layer and whipped cream for the rest.
Super easy to make however I wanted to make homemade brownies versus boxed brownies. Definitely worth the extra effort.

I made mine with less sweetened condensed milk and real dark chocolate for the pudding. It was AMAZING. By the way, I’m one of those few under 12-year-olds that make recipes on this website, including macarons ;) This is a keeper.

This recipe was really good ..I used cool whip in the layers and real whip cream on top…also crushed up Oreos as a layer …everyone loved it for Thanksgiving, And my daughter wanted me to make it again for Christmas!
